status_summary: EO 14173 (signed 2025-01-21) directed agencies to put into every contract and grant a term making compliance with anti-discrimination law material to payment and a certification that the recipient runs no unlawful DEI programs. A GSA FAR class deviation dated 2025-02-15 removed the EO 11246-based clauses from GSA contracts and dropped DEI evaluation factors, and DOJ announced a False Claims Act Civil Rights Fraud Initiative on 2025-05-19. EO 14398 (signed 2026-03-26) required a contract clause barring racially discriminatory DEI activities, and guidance of 2026-04-17 from OFPP, DoD, GSA and NASA put deviation clause FAR 52.222-90 into new solicitations from 2026-04-24 and asked contracting officers to make every effort to modify existing contracts by 2026-07-24. The record is partial: no source was found for the transparency-about-awardees element, and the FAR overhaul is still at the proposed stage.

timeline.event: EO 14173 signed: agencies to include a payment-materiality term and an anti-DEI certification in contracts and grants.
GSA FAR class deviation CD-2025-04 (dated 2025-02-15, made public 2025-02-18) removed EO 11246-based clauses from GSA contracts and DEI evaluation factors; it did not add the new certifications.
EO 14275 signed: OFPP and the FAR Council to rewrite the FAR to keep only required or necessary provisions and to issue deviations meanwhile.
DOJ announced the Civil Rights Fraud Initiative to use the False Claims Act against funding recipients that violate civil rights laws or falsely certify compliance.
EO 14398 signed: contract clause barring racially discriminatory DEI activities; FAR Council to issue deviation guidance within 60 days and amend the FAR.

OFPP, DoD, GSA and NASA issued deviation guidance adding FAR clause 52.222-90; agencies to use it in new solicitations from 2026-04-24 and to make every effort to modify existing contracts by 2026-07-24.
FAR Council published a proposed rule in the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul series covering FAR parts 1, 2, 4, 33, 39, 40, 52 and 53 (comments closed 2026-07-23).

title: Use procurement rules and contract terms to advance policy, including on corporate DEI
uncertainties: The DOJ initiative is sourced to a law firm summary, not the DOJ memorandum itself. The transparency-about-awardees element was not matched to a specific action. The 2026-07-24 date for modifying existing contracts is taken from the April 2026 guidance itself, which resolves a difference between two law firm summaries. Whether the June 2026 proposed rule was the first in the overhaul series was not confirmed. EO 11246 revocation and OFCCP are covered in c18-01 and are not restated.
